incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Companies Act of Taiwan (the Company Act, as amended) Articles 1, 98, 128, 156, 161, 171, 172, 192, 203 and 208; applicable regulations of the Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) for foreign investment approval under the Statute for Investment by Foreign Nationals.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Department of Company Registration, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Taiwan; direct filing through the MOEA Company and Commercial One-Stop Service Portal in Taipei.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Company Incorporation Application Form (公司設立登記申請書) together with the Memorandum of Association and Articles of Incorporation duly executed by all founding shareholders.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-in capital for a limited company under the Taiwan Company Act; however, the capital amount must be sufficient to cover the company's initial operating needs and must be fully subscribed. Paid-in capital is evidenced by bank deposit certificates and certified by a Taiwan CPA for incorporation registration.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: The First Board of Directors Resolution (adopted in writing by unanimous consent of the sole member and sole director on the date of incorporation) resolves: (1) Share Subscription and Capitalization — the founding shareholder subscribes to 100% of the authorized ordinary shares at NTD 1.00 per share; the paid-in capital equal to the amount stated in the incorporation application is deposited in a newly opened corporate bank escrow account in Taiwan and remains at the disposal of the company; (2) Registered Office — the registered office of the company is fixed at the address specified in the Articles of Incorporation, and the company shall file the registered office address with the MOEA Company and Commercial Administration; (3) Officer Appointments — the undersigned appoints the First Director and Chairperson, the General Manager, and the Corporate Secretary, who are each authorized severally to execute incorporation filings, open bank accounts, appoint the Taiwan filing agent, and take all ancillary steps to obtain the business license and operational permits.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Pre-Approval and Foreign Investment Screening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) Company and Commercial One-Stop Service Portal; Investment Commission, MOEA for foreign investment approval.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an online name reservation application for the proposed English and/or Chinese company name. Reserve the name and business scope. Concurrently file a Foreign Investment Application (FIA) with the Investment Commission if the Chinese investor holds any non-resident ownership interest; include audited financial statements or bank reference letters of the foreign investor, a business plan, and the proposed capital remittance schedule. Upon approval, obtain the Foreign Investment Approval Letter.
required_dossiers: Completed Company Name Reservation Application Form
Proposed Articles of Incorporation and Memorandum of Association (draft)
Foreign Investment Application Form and supporting legalization documents of the foreign investor
Bank reference letter or audited financial statements of the foreign investor (if applicable)
Power of Attorney designating the Taiwan filing agent or CPA
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If name reservation is rejected for similarity, file an administrative appeal or amend the name to include a distinctive secondary mark. If the FIA is queried, supplement the required corporate due-diligence documents or narrow the proposed business scope within 14 days to avoid a formal denial.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open Escrow Capital Account and Deposit Paid-In Capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Approved licensed bank in Taiwan with corporate banking authority; foreign exchange bank appointed by the shareholders.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary or escrow corporate bank account in the name of the company to be incorporated ('the company in formation') at the designated Taiwan bank. Remit the agreed paid-in capital from the Chinese investor to the escrow account, complying with cross-border wire documentation and the Central Bank of China (Taiwan) foreign exchange reporting requirements. Upon receipt of the bank certificate (e.g., Deposit Balance Certificate and Debit/Deposit Slip), instruct the CPA to verify the paid-in capital and issue the capital verification report.
required_dossiers: Foreign Investment Approval Letter from the Investment Commission
Name Reservation Certificate
Bank account opening application and KYC documents for the company in formation
Remittance instruction with the purpose of investment
CPA capital verification engagement letter and bank balance certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises KYC concerns or queries the source of funds, provide the required corporate charters, UBO declarations, and board resolutions of the Chinese investor, together with remittance origin documentation. If the remittance is delayed, notify the Investment Commission and apply for an extension of the capital importation period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Notarization of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Taiwan notary public or attorney (notary), followed by filing with the MOEA Company and Commercial Administration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the final Articles of Incorporation and Memorandum of Association in Traditional Chinese with English translation (if required). Ensure the Articles contain the company name, registered office address, business scope, capital structure, share classes, director appointment method, and directors' powers. Have all founding shareholders and the appointed director execute the documents. Authenticate signatures by a Taiwan notary public; if documents originate in Mainland China, arrange notarization by a mainland notary office and subsequent authentication by the Straits Exchange Foundation (SEF) before submission to MOEA.
required_dossiers: Executed and notarized Articles of Incorporation and Memorandum of Association
Power of Attorney for the filing agent/CPA
Notarized certification of shareholder identity documents
SEF authentication certificate for documents originating in Mainland China (if applicable)
Consent of the sole director or first director's acceptance statement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If MOEA rejects the documents for formal defects, resubmit with amendments within 15 days without incurring a new filing fee. If authentication is not finalized, secure a notarial certificate from a Taiwan notary or an alternative overseas chain-authentication route before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Company Incorporation Filing and Business License Issuance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Department of Company Registration, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) — Company and Commercial One-Stop Service Portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the online incorporation application through the One-Stop Service Portal, attaching the CPA capital verification report, Articles of Incorporation, Memorandum, shareholder and director identity documents, and proof of registered office address (e.g., lease agreement or property ownership certificate and landlord's consent). Pay the filing fee (approximately USD 340 equivalent in NTD) electronically. Execute the submission; upon approval, MOEA issues the Company Registration Certificate. Post-approval, register for business tax (sales tax/ VAT) and apply for the Uniform Invoice Number; obtain the business license from the local tax authority (National Taxation Bureau) if required.
required_dossiers: Company Incorporation Application Form (signed by director)
CPA capital verification report and bank deposit certificate
Articles of Incorporation and Memorandum (notarized)
Foreign Investment Approval Letter
Lease agreement or property ownership certificate for the registered office
Identity documents of the director and shareholders
Power of Attorney for the filing agent/CPA
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is suspended or queried, submit a supplementary letter and revised documents within 14 days in accordance with MOEA's notice. If the registration is rejected after two rounds of correction, file a formal administrative appeal to the MOEA Administrative Appeals Committee or reinstate the application by curing the identified defects.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Tax and Social Insurance Registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: National Taxation Bureau (Ministry of Finance) and the Bureau of Labor Insurance / National Health Insurance Administration (Ministry of Health and Welfare).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within 15 days of incorporation, register the company with the National Taxation Bureau for profit-seeking enterprise income tax and uniform invoicing. Apply for the company's Unified Business Number (UBN). Register as an employer with the Labor Insurance Bureau, National Health Insurance Administration, and the Labor Pension Fund Supervisory Commission for mandatory employee insurance contributions. Obtain a certificate of commencement of business operations for the designated PR business scope.
required_dossiers: Company Registration Certificate
Articles of Incorporation and Memorandum
Uniform Invoice Application and business tax registration form
Board resolution appointing the payroll agent and responsible person
Employee roster and labor insurance registration forms (if initial staff is hired)
Lease agreement for the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the taxation bureau questions the business scope or addresses, submit the lease agreement and the company's actual operations plan; if the social insurance authorities identify non-registration of employees, register retroactively and pay late fees to cure the non-compliance.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the overseas public-relations agency does not require industrial or manufacturing licensing under Taiwan's Factory Management Act.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Standard company registration certificate and Uniform Invoice Number; no separate operating license for public-relations consulting under ISIC 7310.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Environmental Protection Administration (EPA, Taiwan), now the Ministry of Environment (MoENV)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — office-based public relations and communication services do not fall within the list of industries subject to environmental impact assessment under the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to an office-based services business; the firm remains subject to general waste-disposal and wastewater-discharge standards under the Waste Disposal Act if it operates any facility, and must comply with relevant indoor air-quality and VOC standards only if it installs printing or media-production equipment exceeding threshold capacity.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The company must obtain a fire-safety certificate for its registered office and any leased office premises from the local fire department, ensure compliance with the Building Act structural and interior-decoration regulations, and maintain a safe workplace under the Occupational Safety and Health Act. Since the firm operates an office environment, it should also complete the General Labor Safety and Health Inspection Checklist and, if applicable, obtain a fire-protection equipment inspection report from a certified fire-safety professional.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance, Taxation Agency (財政部賦稅署) as policy-making authority; operational tax registration is administered by the regional National Taxation Bureaus (各地區國稅局), e.g., the Taipei National Taxation Bureau for Taipei-registered entities. Primary e-services portal: Tax e-Gateway (財政部稅務入口網), www.etax.nat.gov.tw; e-invoice integration platform: www.einvoice.nat.gov.tw; corporate registry gateway: Ministry of Economic Affairs, Department of Commerce (經濟部商業司), www.gcis.nat.gov.tw.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The 8-digit Unified Business Number (統一編號) serves as the single statutory tax ID and is issued automatically upon company incorporation; no separate tax-account application exists. Procedure for a foreign-invested Taiwan JV: (1) obtain investment approval from the Investment Commission under the Ministry of Economic Affairs (Foreign Investment Permission Act; PRC shareholders fall under the Mainland Investment Permission Act with added restrictions); (2) file company incorporation (有限公司 or 股份有限公司) with the central or special-municipality registry, which electronically notifies the competent National Taxation Bureau and triggers simultaneous tax registration (稅籍登記) and VAT-registration status under Business Tax Act Article 28; (3) after incorporation, apply for the MOEA company digital certificate (工商憑證) enabling e-filing and e-invoice transmission. A foreign enterprise without a Taiwan entity or fixed place of business must instead apply for a withholding-unit tax ID (扣繳單位統一編號) at the regional National Taxation Bureau to fulfill Taiwan-source income withholding and reporting obligations; such an enterprise does not obtain VAT registration unless it maintains a fixed place of business or PE in Taiwan.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections exist under Taiwan law. Statutory elections and relief mechanisms available: (a) 10-year net operating loss carryforward under Income Tax Act Article 39, available only to corporations with audited financial statements and approved shareholders' minutes; (b) foreign income tax credit election under Income Tax Act Article 3(2) for overseas-source income taxed abroad, subject to the per-country credit limitation; (c) deemed-profit-rate election under Income Tax Act Article 25 for foreign enterprises providing technical or consulting services in Taiwan where cost allocation is impracticable, subject to Ministry of Finance approval; (d) voluntary VAT registration election for small-scale service businesses whose average monthly sales fall below the NT$40,000 exemption threshold (Business Tax Act Article 13), allowing input VAT credit entitlement.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taiwan Value-Added and Non-Value-Added Business Tax, 加值型及非加值型營業稅法)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: NT$40,000 average monthly sales over a rolling year for service businesses (including PR, advertising and communications agencies) and NT$80,000 for goods-selling businesses. Any business reaching or exceeding the applicable threshold must complete tax/VAT registration before commencing supply (Business Tax Act Article 28). Foreign enterprises with a fixed place of business, branch or agent in Taiwan are registrable regardless of turnover; below-threshold businesses are classified as small-scale taxpayers, exempt from output VAT but ineligible to claim input VAT credits.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Nationwide mandatory e-invoice (電子發票) issuance fully phased in by 2022 for all VAT-registered businesses. Taiwan does not operate real-time transactional pre-clearance by the tax authority; however, all e-invoice records must be transmitted to the Ministry of Finance E-Invoice Integration Service Platform within 48 hours of issuance for both B2B and B2C transactions. High-volume issuers must integrate via direct platform APIs (SOAP/REST web services) or government-certified value-added network providers. B2C receipts carry a QR-code random code (隨機碼); B2B invoices must reference the counterparty's Unified Business Number. Failure to upload within the 48-hour window triggers late-filing penalties, risks disallowance of input VAT credits, and may lead to audit flags.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies under Business Tax Act Article 7 to: (1) exported goods; (2) services supplied in Taiwan for use abroad or services connected with export transactions; (3) services rendered to foreign clients (clients having no fixed place of business in Taiwan) where consideration is received in foreign currency and the proceeds are remitted into Taiwan and settled through an authorized-dealer bank. A global PR and communications agency qualifies at 0% for overseas media-relations and crisis-communication retainer fees paid by foreign principals when the written contract, service-delivery evidence, and bank foreign-exchange settlement records substantiate the cross-border supply. Services supplied to Taiwan-resident clients or performed for local use are standard-rated at 5%; where the supplier is a foreign enterprise without Taiwan registration, the Taiwan buyer must self-assess the 5% business tax by reverse charge.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (出口報單) evidencing goods export clearance through the Customs Administration electronic system
General Uniform Invoice (統一發票) issued at zero rate with the applicable transaction and zero-rating code
Bill of Lading or Airway Bill (提單/航空運單) as physical movement evidence
Bank Foreign Exchange Inward Remittance and Settlement Certificate (外匯收入水單/結售水單) proving receipt and conversion of foreign currency through an authorized-dealer bank in Taiwan
Executed service contract, statements of work, delivery reports, and media-placement or crisis-communication performance records (for services zero-rating)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rated claims are audited against customs export declarations (goods) and bank FX settlement records (services), with cross-checks against the counterparty's residence and the substance of service delivery. Where zero-rating is disallowed, the tax authority retroactively assesses the 5% output VAT with daily interest on the underpaid tax, imposes a penalty of up to five times the tax evaded, may order suspension of the business license (Business Tax Act Article 51), and reassesses income tax with additional Penalty Act surcharges. Knowingly false claims—such as fabricated remittance certificates, fictitious foreign clients, or inflated foreign-currency amounts—constitute tax evasion under Tax Collection Act Article 41, punishable by imprisonment of up to five years, detention, or a fine of up to NT$6 million, and the assessment period for fraudulent under-filing is extended to seven years. Such conduct may also trigger offenses under the Money Laundering Control Act and loss of future zero-rating privileges.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Administration of Foreign Exchange (SAFE) under the People's Bank of China (PBoC); for Taiwan operations, the Central Bank of the Republic of China (Taiwan) (CBC) and Taiwan Financial Supervisory Commission (FSC) are the regulatory counterparts.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Mainland China operates a bifurcated convertibility system under the Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations and SAFE rules. Current account items (e.g., trade in services, advertising and public relations service fees, agency retainers) are generally freely convertible upon verification of genuine underlying transactions. Capital account items (e.g., equity injection, shareholder loans, repatriation of capital) remain subject to registration, approval, or post-transaction filing requirements. For the proposed China-Taiwan JV entity, the principal remittance hurdles are the need to document the commercial reality of each PR retainer and service disbursement, the possibility of a tax treaty rate reduction on dividend or service withholding, and the requirement to route proceeds through a compliant onshore designated foreign exchange account. Taiwan imposes no general restriction on current account convertibility; profits may be repatriated after distribution formalities and satisfaction of withholding tax obligations. Practical friction includes the longer documentary examination cycle for cross-Strait payments, where local banks may apply enhanced scrutiny to remittances referencing 'Taiwan' or 'China' in the beneficiary/purpose fields, and the need to demonstrate that the payments do not constitute prohibited indirect capital flows or unlicensed financial services.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For mainland China, the former mandatory export proceeds surrender system has been liberalized. As of 2012 and subsequent SAFE circulars, enterprises are no longer required to convert export proceeds into CNY at a fixed ratio; instead, foreign exchange receipts may be retained in foreign currency accounts within an approved amount ceiling or settled in CNY according to enterprise preference, subject to the Foreign Exchange Account Quota system. For the JV's PR services exported to overseas clients, receipts must be settled within the prescribed processing period under the SAFE 'trade in services' monitoring framework: enterprises must complete the State Administration of Taxation cross-border receipt verification and SAFE's digital declaration within the time limits set by their bank's 'receipt and payment' control list (generally same-day or T+1 for electronic filings, but the underlying transaction must be fully documented). The statutory requirement is that export receipts of goods and services must be repatriated to China via designated channels and be subject to the 'Who earns, who settles' principle; the actual conversion ratio is 0% mandatory, but the enterprise must justify why the proceeds were not repatriated or were offset against current account liabilities if kept offshore. For Taiwan, there is no forced surrender of export proceeds; exporters may retain earnings in foreign currency accounts at Foreign Exchange Banks (FEBs), subject to declaration if above US$200,000 per year for cross-Strait remittances under the Cross-Strait Banking Supervision Memorandum.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium, with material legal constraints. Offshore digital Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) such as UK FCA-authorised EMIs, Lithuanian EMIs, or multi-currency virtual account providers (e.g., Payoneer, Airwallex, Currencycloud) may be used for collection of retainer fees from global clients, but they are not a substitute for a licensed bank account in mainland China or Taiwan for statutory capital injection, tax payments, VAT issuance, and customs-related banking. Inbound remittances to such EMIs are generally permissible for services exports, but using an EMI to receive payments on behalf of the Chinese JV without a direct underlying client contract may trigger SAFE anti-avoidance review and the EMI's own compliance restrictions. PRC law only recognises payment institution licences issued by the PBoC; foreign EMIs cannot open domestic settlement accounts, cannot issue CNY-denominated accounts for the JV, and any client aggregation or collection from third parties without a legitimate commercial relationship may be deemed illegal payment settlement business under Article 4 of the Administrative Measures for Payment Services of Non-Financial Institutions. The Taiwan side similarly restricts foreign EMI operations: foreign electronic payment institutions must obtain FSC approval for a branch or apply for a third-party payment licence; an unlicensed offshore EMI cannot be used for the JV's local payroll disbursements. The optimum use of an EMI is as a secondary collection rail for foreign-client retainers, with all funds swept within 1-3 business days to the designated onshore bank account, and each use backed by a corresponding service contract and invoice.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: For the mainland China JV, physical presence of directors (or authorized signatories) is mandatory for the initial corporate account opening under the PBoC's 'Knowing Your Customer' requirements and the Anti-Money Laundering Law of the PRC. Most Chinese commercial banks require at least the legal representative (or the authorized representative with a notarized power of attorney) to appear in person at the branch carrying the company's original business licence, official chops (company seal, legal representative seal, finance seal), articles of association, and office lease/proof of actual business premises. Remote account opening is allowed only in limited pilot digital zones (e.g., certain free trade zone banks using cross-border video verification), but such remote opening generally still requires a physical presence at a certified agency or a Chinese-licensed notary once the video verification is completed. For Taiwan, a foreign-invested company has two options: if the JV is registered as a Taiwan branch or a Taiwan company, its Taiwan-appointed manager and the foreign director must appear before the bank manager at the FEB branch; while some Taiwan banks permit video/remote KYC for existing customers, the first account opening for a foreign-owned entity normally requires the responsible person's physical visit or a local attorney-in-fact who carries a valid passport and company registration certificate. The practical mandate is: the Chinese JV legal representative must be physically present at the bank in China; the Taiwan JV manager or designated Taiwan director must be physically present at the bank in Taiwan. No fully remote account opening is available without an existing banking relationship or a specific regulatory pilot waiver.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk cross-strait payment routing and PRC/Taiwan political risk flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide (1) the JV's certificate of incorporation and business license in both Chinese and English; (2) the joint venture contract and any cross-strait investment approvals (e.g., MOFCOM/market supervision filing and Taiwan Investment Commission approval if Taiwan party invests into China); (3) an organizational chart identifying the ultimate beneficial owners (UBOs) with passport copies and residential addresses; (4) a description of the group's PR and communication services, with sample client contracts, to demonstrate no sanctioned or politically exposed activity; (5) a source of funds letter issued by the shareholders' banks covering the initial capital injection; (6) a no-tax-havien declaration if any UBO hold residence in a listed grey jurisdiction; (7) the AML/CFT compliance policy manual of the JV; (8) a board resolution specifically authorizing the account opening, signatories, and participants.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: PRC business scope mismatch — bank sees ISIC 7310 / NAICS 541820 as 'consulting' which may trigger false media/fund-flow red flags
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the exact enterprise business scope ('公关咨询、媒体关系、品牌传播、危机管理、市场推广及配套服务'), a notarized English translation aligning with the ISIC 7310 category 'Advertising and public relations' and NAICS 541820 'Public Relations Agencies', sample campaign retainer agreements, and a SAM (SAFE business codes) classification code for trade in services. Include a comfort letter from the licensed PR association or chamber of commerce confirming the legitimate nature of the firm's services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Capital escrow account initial funding by offshore parent / Taiwan shareholder without clear source-of-funds evidence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare the capital verification report (验资报告) issued by a PRC-certified public accountant, the FDI registration certificate with SAFE, the shareholder's bank reference letter confirming the remitting route, a signed undertaking of the legal shareholder confirming the funds are free of fraud or money laundering, proof of the offshore parent's annual audited financial statements showing the operational source of the contribution, and the board resolution approving the injectant amount.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Processing payments to overseas media vendors and freelance journalists triggers enhanced payment-transaction screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Develop a vendor onboarding file containing each payee's name, jurisdiction, bank, business nature, service agreement, milestones, quotes, invoices, and, where required, an end-buyer declaration. Provide a global media payment matrix and evidence that the JV is not financing terrorism or deceptive malign influence operations. For payees located in high-risk jurisdictions (e.g., offshore financial centers), provide additional beneficial ownership data and a designated compliance officer sign-off.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The initial capital injection from the Taiwan shareholder or other offshore investors into the mainland China JV must comply with the SAFE Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) registration regime. Routeing protocol: (1) obtain the FDI registration certificate with the local SAFE bureau or the delegated bank before opening the capital escrow account; (2) open a Renminbi/Foreign Currency capital account at the designated bank, using the purpose code '622' (FDI capital injection) or the appropriate SAFE code for equity investment; (3) the remittance should be sent by corporate bank transfer, with the remitter's account name matching the shareholder of record, and the wire message must state the purpose as 'capital contribution toward registered capital of [JV name] under FDI approval [number]' and reference the SAFE FDI Registration Code; (4) upon receipt, the bank will verify the amount against the registered capital quota, and the funds must be used within the scope approved by SAFE, generally for operating expenses, purchase of goods/services, or payment of wages; direct conversion of foreign currency capital into CNY is allowed with no mandatory conversion ratio, but any use for entrusted loans, real estate development beyond scope, or fixed-asset investment may require additional registration; (5) the JV must perform the SAFE outbound declaration within the statutory timeline and preserve the bank receipts, capital verification report, and payment instructions for at least five years. If the JV later increases capital, a separate SAFE registration must be amended before the new injection. For the Taiwan JV side (if capital flows from China into Taiwan), the same routeing logic applies under the Taiwan Ministry of Economic Affairs Investment Commission approval, and the remittance should use the purpose code 'ROI: Investment in Taiwan' with a hard copy of the approved plan and the FEB's prior e-declaration.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For cross-border payments of trade settlements, retainer fees, media-buying disbursements, and vendor payments, the following clearing rails are permissible: (1) SWIFT MT103 for direct bank-to-bank wire transfers where the JV's onshore bank transmits to the overseas beneficiary bank, using purpose codes under the SAFE 'Current Account- Trade in Services' (e.g., code '217' for media, public relations, and communication services) and the OECD/UN 'Service' codes; the bank will validate the e-tax invoice (fapiao) and the contract; (2) Commercial Letter of Credit (L/C) is permissible where the JV acts as importer of services or goods for PR production (e.g., production equipment or licensed broadcast materials), with the issuing bank in China/Taiwan and the beneficiary's confirming bank; however, L/C is less common for recurring retainer payments and may be used only for high-value project milestones; (3) Cross-border RMB clearing through the CIPS (Cross-Border Interbank Payment System) and the Taiwan RMB clearing mechanism is allowed for CNY-denominated settlements with counterparties in Taiwan, particularly for fees paid to Taiwanese media agencies; this route requires the Taiwan counterparty to maintain a RMB account at a Taiwanese foreign exchange bank; (4) For payroll and local expenses in Taiwan, the JV should use Taiwan's domestic clearing rails (CHIPS in Taiwan / FEB interbank transfer) after converting CNY/USD into TWD; the conversion is unregulated at the bank level but must be evidenced for tax and audit purposes. All outbound trade disbursements must cross the bank's anti-money-laundering screening; the JV should maintain a robust evidence pack including the fully signed service agreement, itemized invoice, delivery/publish results report, tax withholding certificates, and if above a bank threshold (often USD 50,000), a copy of the SAFE payment certificate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore CNY/USD forward contracts with a licensed PRC bank, permissible only for hedging the JV's genuine current account or capital account exposure (IAS 39 / ASC 815 trade documentation required; no speculative forwards).
Taiwan USD/TWD deliverable forward contracts through a Taiwan FEB, for hedging the Taiwan branch's retained earnings and media procurement exposure.

CNY/TWD non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) offered by offshore banks (mainly in Hong Kong or Singapore), permissible for managing CNY/TWD risk if the JV has no natural CNY/TWD exposure and requires an underlying demonstrable forecast; risk: NDF settlement in USD may create a separate tax/bookkeeping event.

Cross-currency swaps (CNY/USD or TWD/USD) with a licensed bank for matching longer-duration service contracts where the JV has a multi-year retainer in one currency and operating costs in another; only cost-neutral hedging with underlying debt or receivable exposure is permissible.

Currency options (limited, bank discretion) for structured hedging of tender/retainer payments in emerging-market client currencies; due to regulatory restrictions on PRC banks' options salesbooks, these will likely be executed on the Taiwan books where FSC regulations permit plain-vanilla options for professional investors.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Approval of annual financial statements at the shareholders' meeting (or lawful written consent for a closely-held JV) and execution of signed minutes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Company Registration Office; executed minutes maintained at the Taiwan registered office and filed only if the resolution includes a registrable change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Meeting must be held within 6 months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year entity, by June 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Directors may be subject to NT$10,000–NT$100,000 administrative fines; the MOEA may order compliance and shareholders may petition for court-convened meetings

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual final accounts filing, comprising business report, financial statements and profit-distribution or loss-appropriation proposal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA), Company Registration Office, via the MOEA online company registration and filing system
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after fiscal year-end; for a calendar-year entity, no later than June 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to file after notice attracts a NT$20,000–NT$100,000 fine and may lead to formal investigation; administrative strike-off may only follow proof of business inactivity under Company Act Article 10

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual operations and financial information report for the approved foreign/China-invested enterprise
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Investment Commission, Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA-IC)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the close of the fiscal year; for a calendar-year foreign JV, by June 30 of the following year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Investment Commission may issue a correction order, suspend investment approval rights, or recommend revocation of the investment permission in cases of repeated non-filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual profit-seeking enterprise income tax return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Local tax bureau, Ministry of Finance, National Taxation Administration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: May 31 of the following tax year, or the first business day thereafter if the statutory date falls on a weekend or national holiday
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty up to NT$1,500 plus 15% of underpaid tax when the return is filed after an official demand; late payment interest accrues monthly and unpaid taxes are subject to seizure, administrative enforcement, and overseas-travel restriction

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For a non-public Taiwan company, CPA-audited financial statements are compulsory when paid-in capital exceeds NT$30 million (approximately USD 1 million), when the company issues registered securities, or when MOEA orders an audit; the ordinary low-risk PR agency JV remains audit-exempt unless one of those thresholds is crossed
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Public companies apply Taiwan IFRS/TIFRS; non-public small and medium enterprises may apply the Enterprise Accounting Standard (EAS) or TIFRS. All books and vouchers must comply with the Commercial Accounting Act, which also requires preservation of ledgers and financial statements for at least 10 years

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Taiwan does not impose a standalone annual UBO re-filing; the company must update beneficial-owner and shareholding information with MOEA within 15 days of any share transfer or control change, and the register of members must be reconciled at each annual shareholders' meeting. The JV should still perform an internal annual review of its UBO register against bank KYC records and the latest shareholding register

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 800 – 1,500 per year for a Taipei-based corporate agent or registered-office service for an SME foreign JV
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,500 – 7,500 per year for a low-risk PR and communications agency if a statutory audit is required or the Chinese parent group mandates an independent audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No sector-specific tax holidays for public relations agencies. General incentives include research and development investment tax credits, investment in smart machinery or 5G systems, and a reduced branch/retained earnings surtax. The effective rate may be reduced to 12% for taxable income not exceeding NT$120,000, subject to the qualified small-enterprise threshold.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Profit-Seeking Enterprise Income Tax Settlement Return (營利事業所得稅結算申報書) filed through the Taiwan Tax e-Filing Portal (財政部電子申報繳稅服務網站).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual; provisional tax payments are required during the fiscal year in quarterly intervals under Article 67 of the Income Tax Act.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual settlement return must be filed within five months after the fiscal year end. For calendar-year taxpayers, the statutory filing window is 1 May through 31 May.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Gross business revenue (sales, fee income, retainer and commission for PR services).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report Taiwan-source revenue only; revenue attributable to a Taiwan permanent establishment is included.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net business income after deductible costs and expenses, reconciled to audited financial statements.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the arm's-length principle and maintain transfer pricing documentation for intra-group service fees.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after tax-exempt items and prior-year loss carryforward.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident filers may compute apportioned taxable income using the arm's-length allocation for the Taiwan PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of the statutory 20% rate and calculation of provisional tax credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Unless the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement relief is mutually confirmed, the 20% rate applies to the taxable income of the Taiwan PE without gross-basis reduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of related-party transactions and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the transfer pricing schedule if annual related-party transactions exceed NT$200 million or income exceeds NT$3 billion.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: a surcharge of 10% of the underpaid tax if filed after the deadline but before audit notice. Late payment: a monthly surcharge of 1% of the tax due, capped at 15%. Failure to file after an assessment order triggers an additional 10% administrative penalty; directors may be jointly liable for willful evasion.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 20% for dividends paid by a Taiwan profit-seeking enterprise to a non-resident foreign corporate shareholder. A 21% rate applies to non-resident individual shareholders.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Taiwan does not have a conventional double tax agreement because it is not a recognized sovereign state. A Cross-Strait Tax Agreement signed with Mainland China exists but is not fully implemented for operational relief. To invoke any prospective limitation on withholding, the mainland China shareholder must file a beneficial ownership declaration and obtain a Chinese Tax Resident Certificate, then request mutual agreement relief through the Taiwan tax authority; in practice, full domestic statutory withholding is normally applied unless advance permission is obtained.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding is 20% for royalties paid to non-resident corporations and 20% for interest paid to non-resident corporations. No reliable treaty rate is currently available under the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement; domestic statutory rates therefore prevail.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File is mandatory where annual related-party transactions exceed NT$200 million. Master File and Country-by-Country Report are required where the entity's aggregate revenue exceeds NT$3 billion and related-party transactions exceed NT$200 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Taiwan applies the functional substance-over-form doctrine. A JV entity in Taiwan must evidence substantive staff, premises, and decision-making functions to support its transfer pricing positions and to avoid being recharacterised as a conduit or permanent establishment of the mainland China parent. While Taiwan does not apply Caribbean-style Economic Substance Regulations, the Revenue Service denies benefits to shell companies lacking real business purpose, and the application of the Cross-Strait Tax Agreement, if any, is conditioned on genuine economic activity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating service revenue from mainland China clients through fictional offshore intermediaries or suppressing cash wire receipts from the PR agency retainer book.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: A surcharge of up to 2.5 times the underpaid tax, plus a criminal fine and imprisonment of up to five years under the Tax Evasion and Punishment Act.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who orchestrate deceptive invoicing are personally liable for the unpaid tax, face travel bans, attachment of personal assets, and imprisonment; the corporate veil can be pierced upon proof of intentional abuse of the JV entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Creating the Taiwan JV solely to route international PR retainers to avoid mainland China taxes, with no real staff, office infrastructure, or substantive communication activity in Taiwan.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment with a 20% additional tax on recharacterised profits, plus a penalty of 1.5 times the additional tax; denial of treaty or cross-strait relief; possible deregistration of the Taiwan branch.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be compelled to restore diverted profits to the tax authority, prohibited from leaving Taiwan pending investigation, and subject to receiver orders on personal assets if they signed false substance declarations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using inflated public relations retainers or backdated agency agreements to launder funds or to fraudulently convert corporate earnings into deductible expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering penalties under the Money Laundering Control Act: imprisonment up to seven years, fines up to NT$50 million, and confiscation of illicit proceeds; tax fines for falsified invoices up to NT$1 million per violation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors with knowledge of the laundering structure face criminal joint liability and civil restitution to the defrauded tax authority; in severe cases, a permanent departure ban is imposed pending full repayment.
